chapter: Brawls, the Ink Spots and boyhood recollections
title: Flu epidemic in Nashville and curing his mother
summary: His carnival was quarantined in Nashville in the flu epidemic, and at home in Louisville he cured his sick mother with whiskey, glycerine and rock candy.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: And I want to get you back to where this carnival that I was with had traveled to Nashville, Tennessee, and that's when the big epidemic of the flu was around and the show was quarantined in Nashville and we were lucky to get out of Nashville over the quarantine -- a hundred however got out and I went back home to Louisville. When I got into Louisville I found my mother had been sick and a fella on the show that I was with on the carnival, I've forgotten his name, doggone it, can't think of his name. However, he says what I could get -- he showed me what he used for
*The better-known Ink Spots began as a group of four young men in the mid-1930s.

people getting colds in his mother's age and it was good and he said the soldiers use it and it was rock candy, glycerine and whiskey. So I went back to Louisville and my mother was in bed and been in bed for two weeks and I didn't know it. So I made a fire in the stove, we were using coal then, you know, and I went to the liquor store, I got half a pint of whiskey, went to the drug store and got a bottle of glycerine and some rock candy and I brought that back home and gave it to my mother. She got a big dose of that, like a wine glass, I get about three of them and the next day my mother was up and out, you know. I never forgot about that as long as I live. I said the Good Lord brought me back there with my mother then -- instead of me going off with the show then, I went on with the government building highways.
